item.title: Noise-resilient training of machine learning interatomic potentials
item.description:
📚 The Journal of Chemical Physics Current Issue
The accuracy of machine learning interatomic potentials suffers from reference data that contain numerical noise. Often originating from unconverged or inconsistent electronic-structure calculations, this noise is challenging to identify. Existing mitigation strategies, such as manual filtering or iterative refinement of outliers, require either substantial expert effort or multiple expensive retraining cycles, making them difficult to scale to large datasets. Here, we introduce a noise-resilient training method that automatically down-weighs noisy samples, without requiring additional reference calculations. By tracking the loss distribution via an exponential moving average, this unsupervised method identifies outliers throughout a single training run. We show that this approach prevent…

item.title: From nonmagnetic to magnetic: A 2D semiconductor with electrically tunable magnetism
item.description:
📚 Physics News
Researchers from the National University of Singapore (NUS), in collaboration with scientists from institutions in Switzerland, the Czech Republic and Germany, have demonstrated a way to introduce magnetism into an otherwise nonmagnetic two-dimensional (2D) semiconductor and subsequently control its magnetic properties using an electrical voltage. The findings, published in Science Advances, establish a new platform for investigating electrically controllable magnetism in atomically thin materials, with potential implications for future spintronic technologies.

item.title: Adversarial Robustness of Quantum Supervised Learning for Network Intrusion Detection: White-Box Attacks, PGD-Aware Training, and Classical Benchmarking
item.description:
📚 Preprints
👤 Rahul Bhoge, Ranjit Keole, Pravin Karde
Quantum supervised learning (QSL) is increasingly investigated for intrusion detection, yet its behavior under adversarial manipulation remains insufficiently characterized in network-security settings. This study presents a controlled white-box evaluation of a four-qubit variational QSL intrusion detector and a matched classical multilayer perceptron (MLP) on the UNSW-NB15 benchmark.
